text:
Maria G: Heads-up — BeaconMed flagged a month-end mismatch. Dashboard shows $2,120.00 total but invoice INV-2026-03-31-4721 charged $3,580.00. They say a plan tier jumped on 3/31 around cutoff. Can someone triage?
Billing Bot: Automated alert: invoice_delta_detected account=acct_beacon_003 delta=145% threshold=50%
Josh L: Thanks Maria. Can you paste the invoice line items and the dashboard snapshot (CSV or link)? Need account id + billing timezone.
Maria G: Account: acct_beacon_003. Dashboard export (screenshot attached in thread). Key oddity: two plan-tier lines for Mar 31 — one standard plan line and one "provisional premium" line for ~1.2M tokens. No manual change recorded in admin.
Anika P: Running quick metering check for acct_beacon_003 for 2026-03-31 00:00-23:59 UTC. Query: ```sql
SELECT meter_bucket, plan_id, sum(tokens) as tokens
FROM usage_events
WHERE account_id='acct_beacon_003' AND ts >= '2026-03-31' AND ts < '2026-04-01'
GROUP BY 1,2;
```
Anika P: Results: standard_plan: 1,200,120 tokens; premium_plan: 1,100,450 tokens. That looks like double attribution around 23:59:58 UTC.
Samir R: Did they perform a plan upgrade via the customer portal? Admin audit shows no manual upgrade for that account on 3/31.
Priya C: Customer success confirms no self-serve change. They emailed support at 00:02 complaining about spike.
Josh L: Possible explanation: a late-day migration job that reclassified ongoing streams into a fallback premium plan for requests that retried during the cutoff window. We saw a similar pattern in Feb for another account but not identical.
Anika P: I checked request traces for 23:59:45-00:00:15 UTC. There's a batch of long-running streamed responses where the route fallback retried after a soft-oom and were attributed to the active routing policy (premium) instead of original (standard). Logs: ```
TRACE acct_beacon_003 req=0x9a3f fallback_route=premium reason=kv_cache-oom original_route=standard ts=2026-03-31T23:59:56.873Z
```
Maria G: So tokens consumed before cutoff were split between standard and premium because retries closed after midnight? That would explain dashboard showing only standard (it samples pre-cutoff) while invoice summarizes post-rollup which includes retried tokens.
Samir R: Root cause hypothesis: routing fallback increments usage against the new plan_id when the retry crosses the metering window boundary. Metering merge job then aggregates both plan_ids into invoice lines which made the premium line dominant.
Josh L: Repro steps I suggest: 1) spin up a long-stream request under standard plan, 2) force soft-oom on node so fallback triggers, 3) schedule it to straddle 23:59:50 UTC, 4) run end-of-day rollup. If we reproduce, we need a fix to ensure retries attribute to original plan_id or lock metering attribution to request start plan.
Anika P: Quick patch idea: during rollup, detect pairs of events with same request_id and assign tokens to the earliest plan_id. I'll test on a staging dataset.
Priya C: Customer asked for an interim credit while you investigate. They want the delta removed from the invoice if we confirm bug.
Maria G: Can we issue a temporary credit for INV-2026-03-31-4721 pending root cause? CS asks for ETA today.
Josh L: If Anika can repro on staging within an hour, we'll approve a one-time credit and trigger an invoice adjustment.
Anika P: Repro attempt queued on staging. I'll post logs and a minimal SQL diff when done.
Samir R: FYI tagging billing-team for audit: @billing-team please review rollup attribution logic and block similar rollouts until we have a fix.
Billing Bot: Billing audit ticket created: TICKET-6482 assigned=billing-team priority=high
Maria G: Thanks all. I'll update BeaconMed with a short status note (we're investigating, possible retry attribution bug, may issue credit). :thumbsup:
Josh L: Thanks — keep thread updated. If staging repros, we escalate to a postmortem and follow-up customer comms.
